**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, MECA-79 (HEV-specific)+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its proven efficacy in clearing dense, intact lymphoid organs (2-3 mm lymph nodes) while preserving antibody-based fluorescence. Its organic solvent-based delipidation provides deep clearing and high refractive index matching, ideal for 3D light-sheet imaging of vascular networks. The labeling strategy uses CD31 (pan-endothelial marker) to outline all vessels, MECA-79 (a well-established antibody for peripheral node addressing, PNAd, on HEVs) for specific HEV visualization, and Hoechst to label nuclei, providing spatial reference for lymphocyte-dense zones (cortex/paracortex) and overall tissue architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Permeabilization, Blocking, and Immunostaining
1.1 Wash fixed lymph node in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx) for 1 hour at room temperature (RT) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation in permeabilization/blocking solution: PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 2.3% (wt/vol) glycine for 1 day. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation in blocking solution: PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) for 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Incubation in primary antibody cocktail: Rabbit anti-CD31 (1:200) and Rat anti-MECA-79 (1:100) diluted in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 3% (vol/vol) NDS (PBTwDNDS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
1.5 Wash sample in PBTwDNDS 4 times, 1 hour each wash, then overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: ~24 hours total)
1.6 Incubation in secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Donkey anti-Rat Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) diluted in PBTwDNDS. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
1.7 Wash sample in PBTwDNDS 4 times, 1 hour each wash, then overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: ~24 hours total)
1.8 Incubation in nuclear stain solution: 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBTwDNDS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.9 Wash sample in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBTw) 3 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol (MeOH)/PBTw series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) MeOH, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)
2.2 Incubation in fresh 100% (vol/vol) MeOH overnight. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.3 Incubation in 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% (vol/vol) MeOH for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes, twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Transfer cleared lymph node to fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素), CD31 (PECAM1), Podoplanin (PDPN), Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides excellent transparency and shrinkage for small, dense lymphoid tissues like lymph nodes (2-3 mm), enabling deep imaging. It preserves fluorescence well for antibody labeling and small molecule dyes. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: **Lectin** (e.g., UEA-1) binds to glycans on HEV endothelial cells, marking the addressin-rich luminal surface. **CD31** is a pan-endothelial marker to visualize the entire vascular network. **Podoplanin (PDPN)** marks lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs), crucial for distinguishing HEVs from lymphatic sinuses and defining the paracortical zone. **Hoechst** labels all nuclei, allowing for analysis of lymphocyte distribution and cellular density gradients. This combination allows for the simultaneous, specific discrimination of HEVs (Lectin+/CD31+/PDPN-), general blood vasculature (Lectin-/CD31+/PDPN-), and lymphatic sinuses (Lectin-/CD31+/PDPN+).

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Labeling
1.1 Wash fixed and post-fixed inguinal lymph node sample in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin from cold water fish skin in PBS-Tx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200), Armenian Hamster anti-mouse Podoplanin (1:200), and Biotinylated UEA-1 Lectin (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash in PBS-Tx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), Donkey anti-Armenian Hamster IgG Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500), and Streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Wash in PBS-Tx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with nuclear stain: 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.8 Wash in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 15 minutes)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with Dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: Until sample is fully transparent and settled, minimum 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Anti-CD31 (PECAM1) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, Anti-Podoplanin (PDPN) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing capability and high transparency in small, dense lymphoid tissues (2-3 mm LN), enabling deep 3D imaging. It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes well. The labeling strategy targets: 1) CD31 to label all blood vessels, including High Endothelial Venules (HEVs); 2) Podoplanin (PDPN) to specifically label lymphatic endothelial cells and fibroblastic reticular cells, delineating the cortical and paracortical stromal network; 3) Hoechst to label all nuclei, defining lymphocyte-dense zones (cortex/paracortex) and the medulla. This combination allows precise spatial mapping of HEVs relative to lymphocyte zones and stromal scaffolds.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Staining
1.1 Wash fixed lymph node sample in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)
1.2 Blocking in PBS-T containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 1% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200) and hamster anti-mouse Podoplanin (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash in PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-hamster IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Wash in PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
1.7 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Final wash in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Gradual dehydration in a series of tert-butanol (tB) solutions: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol in H2O).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
2.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

3  uDISCO Clearing and RI Matching
3.1 Incubation in a 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and tert-butanol (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 1 hour)
3.3 RI matching and clearing by incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4  Mounting and Imaging
4.1 Mount the cleared lymph node in a chamber filled with fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)
4.2 Image using a light-sheet or confocal microscope equipped with appropriate lasers (405 nm for Hoechst, 561 nm for Alexa Fluor 555, 640 nm for Alexa Fluor 647).

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, PNAd (MECA-79)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is selected because it is a highly effective solvent-based clearing method optimized for fluorescence preservation, especially for Alexa Fluor dyes in fixed tissues. It provides excellent delipidation and transparency for small, dense lymphoid organs (2–3 mm lymph nodes) while maintaining antigenicity. The methanol and DCM steps efficiently remove lipids and reduce autofluorescence. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-CD31 marks pan-vascular endothelium, Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-PNAd (MECA-79) specifically labels HEV addressins, DAPI provides nuclear reference for lymphocyte zones, and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated IB4 lectin broadly labels vascular endothelium (including HEVs) and helps visualize vessel lumen structure, serving as an additional vascular reference and aiding in the identification of lymphocyte-rich areas through vessel density patterns. This multi-channel approach ensures robust, specific signal with minimal background.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated once)  

2  Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  
2.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

3  Immunostaining  
3.1 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  
3.3 Blocking with PBTx containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in blocking solution: rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200), rat anti-mouse PNAd (MECA-79, 1:100), and IB4 lectin (1:50).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.5 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  
3.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in blocking solution: donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-rat IgM Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 555 (for IB4, 1:500).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
3.7 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)  
3.8 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.9 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  

4  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
4.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated once)  
4.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated once)  

5  Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
5.2 Transfer cleared lymph node to fresh DBE for storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD169 (Siglec-1)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous, hydrophilic clearing method that is highly effective for large, dense lymphoid organs like the spleen. It provides excellent transparency and minimal tissue deformation, which is critical for preserving the 3D architecture of B cell follicles and their spatial relationships within the white pulp. CUBIC is compatible with antibody labeling (including after clearing) and preserves the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes very well. The chosen markers directly address the scientific goal: B220 (a pan-B cell marker) will label all B cells and define the follicles; CD169 (marginal metallophilic macrophage marker) will delineate the marginal zone, a key anatomical boundary between red and white pulp; and DAPI will provide a nuclear counterstain for overall cellular density and tissue structure reference.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC-L)**  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% Quadrol, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) for 1 day. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L reagent for 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
1.3 Replacement with fresh 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-L reagent for an additional 3 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

2  **Wash and Antibody Staining**  
2.1 Rinse tissue 3 times with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
2.2 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 for 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Rat anti-mouse B220 (1:200) and Rat anti-mouse CD169 (1:200) in blocking solution for 5 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 120 hours)  
2.4 Wash tissue 6 times with PBST over 2 days, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Donkey anti-Rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution for 5 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 120 hours)  
2.6 Wash tissue 6 times with PBST over 2 days, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.7 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS for 2 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.8 Final wash in PBS 3 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

3  **Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)**  
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ reagent (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in dH2O, RI ~1.49) for 1 day. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ reagent for 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Replacement with fresh 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ reagent for final equilibration and storage until imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC), Lectin (IB4), DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its excellent clearing of dense lymphoid organs like spleen, strong compatibility with whole-organ immunolabeling, and robust preservation of endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence. It effectively handles the size of a fixed mouse spleen (15x10x5 mm). The labeling strategy uses B220 (a pan-B cell marker) to identify all B cells and follicles, and the lectin IB4 (which binds to α-D-galactosyl residues enriched in germinal center follicular dendritic cells) as an auxiliary marker for germinal center-like regions. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for assessing cellular density and overall architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

2  Delipidation and Bleaching
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

3  Rehydration and Blocking
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Wash with PBS-T three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
3.6 Incubation in blocking solution (PBS-T with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M Glycine, 6% (wt/vol) Donkey Serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

4  Immunolabeling and Lectin Staining
4.1 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing anti-B220 antibody (e.g., Rat anti-mouse CD45R, 1:200) and biotinylated IB4 Lectin (e.g., 10 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
4.2 Wash with PBS-T six times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours each)
4.3 Secondary antibody and streptavidin incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
4.4 Wash with PBS-T six times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours each)
4.5 Nuclear staining: Incubation in PBS-T containing DAPI (1 µg/mL). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.6 Wash with PBS-T three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)

5  Dehydration for Clearing
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS-T. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

6  Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching
6.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, until tissue is clear and sinks)

7  Storage and Imaging
7.1 Store cleared spleen in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at RT until imaging. (Temperature: RT)
7.2 For imaging, mount sample in a chamber filled with DBE suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Justification:** PEGASOS 方法特别适用于完整、富含血红素的器官（如脾脏），其强效的脱色和脱脂步骤能有效去除血红蛋白和脂质，解决样本暗红和背景高的问题。该方法能实现高透明度和低自发荧光，非常适合多通道荧光成像和三维重建。所选标记策略中，B220（CD45R）标记所有B细胞以勾勒滤泡，CD3标记T细胞以区分白髓区域，Ki67标记增殖细胞以识别生发中心，DAPI标记细胞核用于结构定位。此组合可在不引入列表外试剂的前提下，实现B细胞滤泡空间定位和生发中心反应强度的量化分析。

**Protocol Steps:**
1 脱色与脱脂
1.1 样本在脱色液A (4% (wt/vol) 多聚甲醛，4% (wt/vol) 乙二醛，0.01% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PB) 中孵育。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

1.3 样本在梯度脱脂液 (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) 叔丁醇 in ddH2O) 中依次孵育，每步更换新鲜溶液。(Temperature: RT, Time: 每步 12 hours)
1.4 样本在 100% (vol/vol) 叔丁醇中再次孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2 再水化与通透
2.1 样本在梯度叔丁醇溶液 (80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) 叔丁醇 in ddH2O) 中依次孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 每步 6 hours)
2.2 样本在 PBS (含 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) 叠氮化钠) 中洗涤。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)
2.3 样本在通透液 (PBS 含 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) 皂苷, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.05% 叠氮化钠) 中孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

3.2 样本在含一抗混合液 (大鼠抗小鼠 B220 [克隆 RA3-6B2] 1:200，兔抗小鼠 CD3 1:200，兔抗小鼠 Ki67 1:200 in 封闭液) 中孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.3 样本在洗涤液 (PBS 含 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) 皂苷, 0.05% 叠氮化钠) 中洗涤。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 × 2 hours)
3.4 样本在含二抗及核染液混合液 (驴抗大鼠 IgG Alexa Fluor 488 1:500，驴抗兔 IgG Alexa Fluor 647 1:500，驴抗兔 IgG Alexa Fluor 555 1:500，DAPI 1:1000 in 封闭液) 中孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.5 样本在洗涤液 (PBS 含 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) 皂苷, 0.05% 叠氮化钠) 中洗涤。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 × 2 hours)

4 脱水与折射率匹配
4.1 样本在梯度脱水液 (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) 叔丁醇 in ddH2O) 中依次孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 每步 12 hours)

5.1 将透明化样本转移至充满新鲜 DBE 的成像腔室或玻璃皿中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 直至成像)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 647, CD8+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides excellent transparency and shrinkage for dense, lipid-rich tissues like tumors, achieving high refractive index (RI ~1.56) ideal for high-resolution deep imaging. Its organic solvent-based process effectively removes lipids while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes, crucial for analyzing T cell subsets. The chosen labeling strategy uses CD3 to identify all T cells and CD8 to specifically label cytotoxic T cells, allowing for density and spatial distribution analysis. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for defining tissue architecture and cellular density without interfering with specific marker signals.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF) in distilled water.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

2  Immunostaining (Performed after Step 1.4, prior to final dehydration and clearing)
2.1 Blocking and Permeabilization: Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 3% (wt/vol) Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 3% (wt/vol) BSA, and the following primary antibodies: anti-CD3 (1:200, clone 17A2) and anti-CD8α (1:200, clone 53-6.7).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 96 hours)
2.3 Wash: Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)
2.4 Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Stain Incubation: Incubation with PBST containing 3% (wt/vol) BSA, donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500), and Hoechst 33342 (1:1000).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 96 hours)
2.5 Wash: Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)
2.6 Final Dehydration: Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeated twice)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation with Dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: Until tissue is transparent and sinks, typically 3-6 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 488, CD8+Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong shrinkage (preserving tissue architecture while reducing size, beneficial for large 8 mm tumors), maintains excellent fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes over long periods, and is compatible with pre-fixed, antibody-labeled tissues. The method uses tetrahydrofuran (THF) and dibenzyl ether (DBE), which efficiently delipidate and clear dense tumor tissue. CD3 marks all T cells, CD8 marks cytotoxic T cells, and Hoechst defines nuclear architecture to delineate tumor core, edge, and cellular density zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2  Refractive Index Matching  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeat until fully transparent)  

3  Immunostaining (performed before clearing)  
3.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CD3 (1:200, Rabbit) + anti-CD8α (1:200, Rat) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.4 Wash with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  
3.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) + Donkey anti-Rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) + 5 µg/mL Hoechst in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.6 Wash with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  
3.7 Post-fixation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.8 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  

4  Storage and Imaging  
4.1 Store cleared sample in fresh DBE in a light‑tight container.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
4.2 Mount in DBE for light‑sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 488, CD8+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional transparency, high tissue shrinkage resistance (crucial for preserving spatial metrics like distance distribution), and strong compatibility with antibody labeling in whole, fixed tissues of the specified size (~8x8x6 mm). It provides excellent preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes across multiple channels. The labeling strategy uses CD3 (pan-T cell) and CD8 (cytotoxic T cell) to distinguish the required subpopulations. CD31 (PECAM1) provides essential vascular architecture reference. Hoechst is used as a nuclear counterstain for cellular localization and to delineate tissue compartments (e.g., necrotic core). This combination enables precise 3D mapping of T-cell infiltration gradients relative to tumor boundaries and vasculature.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Incubation with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 1% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2  Primary Antibody Staining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse CD3 (1:200), rabbit anti-mouse CD8α (1:200), and goat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

3  Washing after Primary Staining
3.1 Wash with PBS-T six times with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)

4  Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Staining
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibody and nuclear dye cocktail: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500), and Hoechst 33342 (1:1000) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

5  Washing after Secondary Staining
5.1 Wash with PBS-T six times with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)

6  Dehydration
6.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
6.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7  Delipidation and Clearing
7.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM, Sigma 270997) in methanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

8  Refractive Index Matching
8.1 Incubation with Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for refractive index matching and final storage/imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Overnight or until tissue is fully transparent)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 488, CD8+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 750]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected over the previously used iDISCO+ for several reasons critical to the problem statement. It achieves superior transparency in dense, lipid-rich tissues like solid tumors, which is essential for imaging the tumor core. It significantly enhances endogenous fluorescence signals (e.g., GFP, tdTomato) and antibody-conjugated fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor series) through a chemical "fluorescence boosting" step, directly addressing the weak T-cell marker signal. The protocol includes a decolorization step (using H2O2) to reduce autofluorescence from hemoglobin and other pigments, which is crucial for accurate quantitative analysis in tumor tissue. The final refractive index matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI~1.56) is excellent for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses CD3 (pan-T cell) and CD8 (cytotoxic T cell) with spectrally distinct, bright Alexa Fluor dyes to enable dual-population analysis. CD31 marks vasculature for defining perivascular regions, DAPI labels nuclei for segmentation, and Lectin (e.g., IB4) can be used to outline tissue architecture or specific vascular beds if needed, all within the permitted dye list.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Decolorization and Dehydration
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume of 30% H2O2 with 5 volumes of 100% methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours, protected from light)

2  Rehydration and Permeabilization
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)

3  Immunostaining
3.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours with gentle shaking)
3.2 Primary antibody incubation in PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBS-Tw), 3% NDS, and 0.01% sodium azide. Use: anti-CD3 (1:200), anti-CD8 (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:200), Lectin (e.g., IB4, 1:100). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours with gentle shaking)
3.3 Wash with PBS-Tw. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 6 times over 12 hours)
3.4 Secondary antibody and nuclear stain incubation in PBS-Tw with 3% NDS. Use: Donkey anti-Rat Alexa Fluor 488 (for CD3), Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (for CD8), Donkey anti-Hamster Alexa Fluor 555 (for CD31), Streptavidin Alexa Fluor 750 (for Lectin-IB4), and DAPI (1 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours with gentle shaking, protected from light)
3.5 Wash with PBS-Tw. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 6 times over 12 hours, protected from light)

4  Dehydration for Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5  Fluorescence Enhancement and Lipid Removal
5.1 Incubation with a 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeat once)

6  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeat once or until tissue is fully transparent)
6.2 Store cleared sample in fresh DBE in a light-protected container at 4 ℃ until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 (Connexin 43) + Alexa Fluor 647, Purkinje fiber-associated contact protein (e.g., Neurofilament-M or Contactin-2/Cntn2) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing capability and strong preservation of endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence in large, dense organs like the heart. It achieves high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), ideal for deep imaging of a 10 mm sample. The chosen labeling strategy uses specific primary antibodies against Cx43 (a key gap junction protein in the cardiac conduction system) and a Purkinje fiber marker (e.g., Neurofilament-M or Cntn2), conjugated to spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (647 and 488). This allows for precise dual-channel visualization of the two target networks. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context. This combination enables the direct comparison of spatial distribution, overlap, branching patterns, and signal continuity between the Purkinje network and the gap junction-defined conduction system.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed heart sample in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation in PBS-T with 20% (vol/vol) Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO) for enhanced permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Wash sample in PBS-T. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Blocking by incubation in PBS-T containing 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin from cold water fish skin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubate sample in PBS-T with 0.2% gelatin, 5% DMSO, and the following primary antibodies: rabbit anti-Cx43 (1:200) and chicken anti-Neurofilament-M (or mouse anti-Cntn2, 1:200). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)
2.3 Wash sample in PBS-T with 0.2% gelatin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with solution changed every 2 hours)
2.4 Secondary antibody and nuclear stain incubation: Incubate sample in PBS-T with 0.2% gelatin, 5% DMSO, and the following: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-chicken (or anti-mouse) IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and DAPI (1 µg/mL). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)
2.5 Wash sample in PBS-T. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with solution changed every 2 hours)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration by incubating sample in a series of tert-Butanol (tB) solutions: 30% (vol/vol), 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% tB in deionized water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours per step)
3.2 Delipidation by incubation in 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation in Dibenzyl Ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for RI matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours or until optically clear)
4.2 Storage of cleared sample in fresh DBE in a light-tight container until imaging. (Temperature: RT)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40/Hcn4 (for Purkinje fibers), Lectin (for vasculature), Hoechst (for nuclei)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency in whole adult mouse organs (including heart) with minimal tissue shrinkage, excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence, and compatibility with organic-solvent–based refractive-index matching (DBE) for high-resolution light-sheet imaging. The method is robust for 3D reconstruction of fine networks like Purkinje fibers. Cx40/Hcn4 is a well-established marker for cardiac conduction system; lectin provides vascular reference; Hoechst labels nuclei for cellular orientation. This combination allows unambiguous identification of Purkinje fibers against anatomical landmarks.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2  Immunostaining and Labeling  
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PTx.2 (PBS with 0.2% Triton X‑100, 6% donkey serum) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑Cx40 (1:200) and biotinylated lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100) in PTx.2 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PTx.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PTx.2 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PTx.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  
2.6 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (2 µg/mL) in PTx.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PTx.2 (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, 3 changes)  

3  Dehydration for Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  

4  uDISCO Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) BABB‑D (benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate = 1:2, with 0.4% w/v diphenyl ether as antioxidant) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours until transparent)  

5  Refractive‑Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Transfer cleared heart into fresh BABB‑D (Temperature: RT, Time: storage until imaging)  
5.2 Mount sample in imaging chamber filled with BABB‑D for light‑sheet microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Collagen IV+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that preserves fluorescence well and is highly effective for whole-organ clearing of soft tissues like kidney. It achieves high transparency and low autofluorescence, essential for deep imaging of the entire 10 mm kidney. The chosen labeling strategy targets: 1) Nephrin (podocyte slit diaphragm) to specifically label glomeruli; 2) Collagen IV (basement membrane) to outline glomerular and tubular structures; 3) IB4 lectin (binds endothelial glycans) to highlight glomerular capillary loops; 4) DAPI for nuclear counterstain. This multi-channel approach allows precise glomerular identification, 3D segmentation, and volumetric/morphometric analysis in health and disease.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash fixed kidney in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) D‑sorbitol in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunostaining and Labeling  
2.1 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑Nephrin (1:200), goat anti‑Collagen IV (1:200), IB4‑Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST for 24 hours, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti‑goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST for 24 hours, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBST for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC‑R1)  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑R1 solution (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑dimethylformamide (DMF), 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Refresh CUBIC‑R1 solution and continue incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC‑R2)  
4.1 Wash with PBS for 12 hours to remove residual CUBIC‑R1. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with CUBIC‑R2 solution (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''‑nitrilotriethanol in water). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Refresh CUBIC‑R2 solution and incubate until tissue is fully transparent (RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Transfer cleared kidney to imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC‑R2. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
5.2 Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, 555, 647 and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous, hydrophilic clearing method that preserves fluorescence of proteinaceous antigens (like Nephrin and Podocin) exceptionally well and is highly effective for whole-organ clearing of soft tissues like kidney. It enables deep antibody penetration for whole-mount immunolabeling of two key slit diaphragm proteins simultaneously. The use of IB4 lectin labels the vasculature/glomerular endothelium as a structural reference, while Hoechst provides nuclear context. CUBIC's refractive index matching (RI ~1.52) is compatible with high-resolution confocal or light-sheet microscopy for 3D analysis of signal continuity, intensity, and focal loss across glomeruli.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed kidney in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, changing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in distilled water) for passive permeabilization and delipidation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

2  Whole-Mount Immunolabeling
2.1 Wash tissue 3 times in PBST, 2 hours each wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.2 Blocking in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation in PBST containing 1:200 rabbit anti-Nephrin (NPHS1), 1:200 goat anti-Podocin (NPHS2), 1:100 IB4-Alexa Fluor 555, and 5% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)
2.4 Wash tissue 6 times in PBST, 4 hours each wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubation in PBST containing 1:500 donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647, and 5% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.6 Wash tissue 6 times in PBST, 4 hours each wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Nuclear staining: Incubation in PBST containing 1:1000 Hoechst 33342. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.8 Final wash in PBST, 3 times for 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in distilled water, RI ~1.48) for dehydration and initial clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R1 solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (50 wt% antipyrine, 25 wt% nicotinamide, 35 wt% N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine in distilled water, RI ~1.52) for final clearing and RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.4 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R2 solution until tissue is fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours)

4  Mounting and Storage
4.1 Mount cleared kidney in CUBIC-R2 solution within an appropriate imaging chamber (e.g., glass-bottom dish or custom chamber). (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
4.2 For storage, seal chamber and keep in the dark at 4 ℃. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)

**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that provides excellent transparency for whole organs (including kidney), preserves endogenous and antibody-introduced fluorescence well, and is compatible with large tissue volumes (~10 mm). Its two-step reagent system (delipidation/decolorization followed by refractive index matching) effectively clears lipid-rich tissues while maintaining protein epitopes. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: Podocin and Nephrin are definitive podocyte slit‑diaphragm markers; IB4 lectin robustly labels the glomerular capillary lumen/endothelium; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for overall cellular architecture. All four channels can be spectrally separated for simultaneous 3D analysis of podocyte structure, capillary loops, and their spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed kidney (4% PFA) in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) D‑sorbitol in PBST for permeabilization. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2  Immunostaining and Lectin Labeling
2.1 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑Podocin (NPHS2, 1:200) and guinea pig anti‑Nephrin (NPHS1, 1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST, refreshing every 2 hours for a total of 6 washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti‑guinea pig Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and IB4‑Alexa Fluor 555 (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST, refreshing every 2 hours for a total of 6 washes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.6 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.7 Final wash with PBS (without Triton) for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3  Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC‑1)
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑1 reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑dimethylformamide (DMF), 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.2 Refresh CUBIC‑1 reagent and continue incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)

4  Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC‑2)
4.1 Wash tissue in PBS for 12 hours to remove residual CUBIC‑1. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation with CUBIC‑2 reagent (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% triethanolamine, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.3 Refresh CUBIC‑2 reagent and continue incubation until tissue is fully transparent (RI ~1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)

5  Mounting and Imaging
5.1 Transfer cleared kidney to a imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC‑2 reagent. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)
5.2 Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 555, and Alexa Fluor 647.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong tissue shrinkage (up to ~65% volume reduction), which is advantageous for large, blood-rich organs like the liver, as it efficiently removes lipids and pigments while preserving fluorescence. Its organic-solvent-based protocol is compatible with whole-organ clearing and provides excellent refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses CK19 (a specific marker for biliary epithelial cells) to highlight the entire biliary tree, IB4 lectin to label vascular endothelium (providing anatomical reference for portal triads without replacing the primary biliary signal), and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining to identify cellular organization and injury zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

2  Immunostaining (Optional Pre-clearing Staining; if performing post-clearing staining, adjust order)  
2.1 Rehydration through graded methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% methanol in PBS, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T) for 1 hour, repeated three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
2.3 Blocking with PBS-T containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CK19 (1:200) and IB4 lectin (1:100) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T for 1 hour, repeated six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-lectin Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS-T for 1 hour, repeated six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
2.8 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.9 Wash with PBS for 1 hour, repeated three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Dehydration through graded methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  
3.5 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for refractive index matching until tissue is transparent (typically 12-24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4  Storage and Imaging  
4.1 Store cleared liver in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long-term)  
4.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for light-sheet microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its robust clearing of large, dense, and blood-rich organs like the liver, excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (e.g., from potential reporter mice), and compatibility with immunolabeling. The methanol series effectively removes heme pigments (reducing autofluorescence) and lipids. The labeling strategy uses CK19 (a definitive marker for biliary epithelial cells) to specifically identify the ductal network, while Lectin (e.g., *Dolichos biflorus* agglutinin) labels vascular and sinusoidal endothelial, providing a crucial anatomical reference to distinguish ducts from blood vessels. DAPI stains nuclei for cellular localization and tissue architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Immunolabeling
1.1 Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, and 6% Normal Donkey Serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.2 Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 3% Normal Donkey Serum, and primary antibodies (Rabbit anti-CK19, 1:500; Biotinylated *Dolichos biflorus* Lectin, 1:200). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.3 Wash: Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 and 0.05% Tween-20 (PBTw). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)
1.4 Secondary Antibody/Streptavidin Incubation: Incubation with PBTw containing 10% DMSO, 3% Normal Donkey Serum, and detection reagents (Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500; Streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500; DAPI, 5 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.5 Final Wash: Incubation with PBTw. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Methanol Series Dehydration: Sequential incubation in 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
2.2 Delipidation: Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.3 Bleaching (Optional, for fluorescence preservation): Incubation with fresh 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.4 Rehydration: Sequential incubation in 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
3.1 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in Ethyl Cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in Ethyl Cinnamate (ECi). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Final Clearing and RI Matching: Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Ethyl Cinnamate (ECi, RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, then store at 4 ℃ until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC (Clear, Unobstructed Brain/Body Imaging Cocktails) is selected because it is highly effective for large, dense organs like the whole mouse liver, providing excellent delipidation and decolorization while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody labeling. Its aqueous‑based, hydrophilic nature is gentle on tissue structure and compatible with subsequent immunolabeling. The chosen labeling strategy targets: CK19 (a specific marker for biliary epithelial cells) to visualize the entire bile duct network; Lectin (e.g., UEA‑I or Lycopersicon esculentum lectin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 to label vascular endothelium, delineating portal tracts; and DAPI for nuclear counterstain to provide cellular context and aid in portal tract identification. This combination allows simultaneous 3D mapping of bile ducts, portal vasculature, and overall tissue architecture, enabling analysis of ductal expansion along portal tracts, reactive ductular proliferation, and regional remodeling differences.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1  Wash fixed liver (20 mm × 15 mm × 10 mm) in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2  Incubation in 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3  Incubation in 30% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2  Immunolabeling  
2.1  Blocking in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2  Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑CK19 (1:500) and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., UEA‑I, 10 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3  Wash in PBST for 24 hours, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4  Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin‑Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5  Wash in PBST for 24 hours, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6  Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7  Final wash in PBST for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3  Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC‑1)  
3.1  Incubation in CUBIC‑1 reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑dimethylformamide, 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in water) for 7 days, refreshing reagent on day 4. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

4  Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC‑2)  
4.1  Wash in PBS for 12 hours to remove residual CUBIC‑1. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2  Incubation in CUBIC‑2 reagent (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% triethanolamine in water) for 3 days, refreshing reagent on day 2. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)  

5  Mounting and Imaging  
5.1  Transfer cleared liver into a custom‑made or commercial imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC‑2 reagent. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2  Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 488, CK7+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its powerful decolorization and delipidation capabilities, which are critical for the blood-rich, opaque mouse liver. Its organic solvent-based protocol effectively removes heme pigments and lipids, enabling deep imaging. The method is compatible with whole-organ clearing of the specified size and preserves the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes conjugated to antibodies. Using two distinct Alexa Fluor conjugates against CK19 and CK7 allows for comprehensive, dual-channel delineation of the biliary tree, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Wash fixed liver sample in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M Glycine) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) Donkey Serum) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (e.g., Rabbit anti-CK19 and Mouse anti-CK7, each at 1:200-1:500 dilution in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (vol/vol) Donkey Serum (PBS-Tw-DS)) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash sample in PBS-Tw (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20) for 24 hours, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail (e.g., Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 and Donkey anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 647, each at 1:500 dilution in PBS-Tw-DS) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash sample in PBS-Tw for 24 hours, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Optional nuclear staining: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.6 Final wash in PBS-Tw for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Dehydration and Decolorization
3.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series in distilled water: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 hours total)
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 12 hours to complete dehydration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume of 30% H2O2 with 5 volumes of 100% methanol) for 48 hours for thorough decolorization. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

4  Delipidation and Clearing
4.1 Wash in 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour to remove H2O2. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes to remove remaining lipids. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.4 Wash in 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5  Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for RI matching and final clearing. Store and image in DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: Overnight (12-24 hours) until sample is fully transparent)

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and significant tissue shrinkage (up to ~65% in volume), which is advantageous for dense, air-filled organs like the lung, as it compacts the tissue and reduces light scattering. The method preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes well over long periods and is compatible with antibody labeling in whole-mount tissues. α-SMA is the definitive marker for airway smooth muscle; Lectin (IB4) labels endothelial cells and some glycoproteins, outlining vasculature and airway epithelium for structural reference; DAPI labels nuclei for cellular context. This combination allows clear 3D visualization of smooth muscle layers along the entire bronchial tree.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2  Immunostaining (Whole-Mount)  
2.1 Rehydration through graded methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)  
2.3 Blocking with PBS-T containing 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum and 10 µg/mL Lectin (IB4)-Alexa Fluor 488 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Primary antibody incubation: anti-α-SMA antibody (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 4 times)  
2.6 Secondary antibody incubation: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and DAPI (1:1000) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 4 times)  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Dehydration through graded methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), alpha-SMA (primary antibody, e.g., Cy3 conjugate), DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides excellent transparency and high fluorescence preservation for large, fixed tissues like whole lung lobes, which is critical for deep 3D imaging of airway structures. It achieves strong tissue shrinkage, facilitating high-resolution imaging of dense tissue. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin, providing a robust structural reference for airway wall and epithelial architecture. Co-labeling with alpha-SMA (a canonical smooth muscle marker) specifically identifies airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs), enabling precise quantification of ASM layer thickness and coverage. DAPI labels nuclei for cellular context and airway layer demarcation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Immunofluorescence and F-actin Labeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking and permeabilization solution: 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (wt/vol) BSA, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody solution: anti-alpha-SMA antibody (e.g., Cy3 conjugate, 1:200 dilution) in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3% (wt/vol) BSA, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with solution changed every 2 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary labeling solution: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Phalloidin (1:100 dilution) and DAPI (1:1000 dilution) in PBST with 3% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with solution changed every 2 hours)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with clearing solution: Diphenyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, until tissue is transparent)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
4.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh Diphenyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 0 hours, for immediate imaging or storage in the dark at 4 ℃)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS (Revised Protocol)
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA+Alexa Fluor 488, SM22α+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]
**Justification:** The original PEGASOS method is retained but critically revised to address the stated issues. PEGASOS is highly suitable for large, dense organs like lungs, providing excellent clearing depth and structural preservation for 3D analysis. The revisions specifically target the weak signal and uneven clearing: 1) **Extended Delipidation & Decoloration:** Significantly延长 delipidation time and re-introducing the decoloration step are crucial for removing lung pigments (heme) and lipids that cause autofluorescence and uneven RI, which directly improves signal-to-noise and clearing uniformity. 2) **Enhanced Labeling Strategy:** Using two primary antibodies (α-SMA for mature smooth muscle, SM22α for a broader smooth muscle lineage marker) with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes enables comprehensive dual-signal assessment of distribution, thickness, and hyperplasia. Co-staining with IB4 lectin outlines airway/vessel walls and lung innervation (vagal fibers), providing essential structural context. DAPI labels nuclei. This combination, applied *after* clearing and RI matching (as per PEGASOS' "labeling-after-clearing" principle), maximizes antibody penetration and preserves fluorescence in the cleared, accessible tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Decoloration and Delipidation (Critical Revision)
1.1 Incubation with Decoloration Solution (5% w/v thioglycolic acid, pH 7-8, adjusted with NaOH).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)
1.2 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.3 Incubation with Delipidation Solution 1 (25% w/v Quadrol in ddH2O).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, with gentle shaking)
1.4 Wash with PBST 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.5 Incubation with Delipidation Solution 2 (25% w/v N-butyldiethanolamine in ddH2O).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, with gentle shaking)
1.6 Wash with PBST 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

2  Refractive Index (RI) Elevation and Tissue Homogenization
2.1 Dehydration through a graded series of tert-butanol (tB) in ddH2O: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol for 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Benzyl Ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.4 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) Benzyl Ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, until tissue is fully transparent and sinks)

3  RI Matching for Imaging
3.1 Incubation with Benzyl Benzoate (BB) for RI matching (RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Optional: For long-term storage, transfer tissue to a mixture of BB and Benzyl Alcohol (2:1 ratio).(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

4  Immunostaining (Labeling-after-Clearing)
4.1 Rehydration of cleared tissue through a reverse graded series of tB in ddH2O: 100%, 90%, 80%, 70%, 50%, 30%, PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per step)
4.2 Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with Permeabilization/Blocking Buffer (PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, and 3% donkey serum).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, with gentle shaking)
4.3 Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with antibody cocktail in Antibody Dilution Buffer (PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, 3% donkey serum): anti-α-SMA (1:200), anti-SM22α (1:200), IB4-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:100).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7-10 days, with gentle shaking)
4.4 Wash with Wash Buffer (PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100) 6 times over 48 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash)
4.5 Secondary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in Antibody Dilution Buffer: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (for α-SMA, 1:500), Donkey anti-Goat Alexa Fluor 647 (for SM22α, 1:500).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7-10 days, with gentle shaking)
4.6 Wash with Wash Buffer 6 times over 48 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours per wash)
4.7 Nuclear Staining: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.8 Final Wash with PBS 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)

5  Final Clearing and Mounting for Imaging
5.1 Dehydration through graded tB series (as in Step 2.1).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)
5.2 Incubation with 100% tB followed by 100% DBE (as in Steps 2.2-2.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: As per Steps 2.2-2.4)
5.3 Final RI matching in BB or BB/BA mixture (as in Step 3).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.4 Mount the cleared, labeled lung lobe in fresh BB/BA in an appropriate imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that is highly effective for soft, irregular organs like the pancreas, providing excellent transparency and minimal tissue deformation. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets β‑cells (Insulin), provides nuclear reference (DAPI), and outlines vasculature/ducts (Lectin) for spatial context, enabling accurate 3D segmentation and quantification of β‑cell mass, islet number, size distribution, and regional burden.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Delipidation and Decolorization  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑dimethylformamide (DMF), 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 1% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: guinea pig anti‑Insulin (1:500), biotinylated Lectin (e.g., UEA‑I or GSL‑I, 1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑guinea pig Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''‑nitrilotriethanol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)

4 Storage and Imaging  
4.1 Mount sample in fresh CUBIC-R2 within an imaging chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
4.2 For long‑term storage, seal chamber and store at 4 ℃ protected from light (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 month)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin+Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1+Alexa Fluor 647, Somatostatin (SST)+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous, hydrophilic clearing method that is highly effective for soft organs like pancreas, preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence well, and is scalable to the given tissue size (~15 mm). It allows deep antibody penetration for multiplexed labeling of hormones (Insulin, SST) and transcription factors (PDX1). Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for cell/isllet boundary identification. The method is compatible with subsequent whole-mount 3D imaging and volumetric analysis of β-cell mass.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed pancreas in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in distilled water) for passive delipidation and permeabilization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Blocking in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: guinea pig anti-Insulin (1:500), rabbit anti-PDX1 (1:300), goat anti-Somatostatin (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.3 Wash in PBST, refreshing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.5 Wash in PBST, refreshing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final wash in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in distilled water, RI ~1.48) for refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)
3.2 Transfer to CUBIC-R2 (50 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 20 wt% N-methylnicotinamide in distilled water, RI ~1.52) for final clearing and storage. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)
